transcript:
Header: 2026-09-01 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (NexaHealth), Marcus Chen (Nexa SRE), Aisha Patel (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Tuesday. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena: Hey Jordan, Lena here.
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus, on the line.
[00:10] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood.
[00:14] Jordan: Cool. I'll kick us off, agenda — quick onboarding status, access/VPC check, go over last week's benchmark snippets, tuning suggestions (quantization & batch), and then next steps. Anything to add?
[00:25] Aisha: Maybe a short ask on security docs, whether SOC2 stuff updated?
[00:28] Jordan: Yep we'll touch on that — Priya has the list.

[00:36] Jordan: Onboarding — where do we stand? Marcus?
[00:40] Marcus: We've created the service account keys but hit a snag with VPC peering. Our infra team needs the subnet IDs and a proposal for routes. I put the peering request in but awaiting details. Also we tried the sample token exchange and saw 401 intermittently, might be a creds issue or clock skew.
[01:05] Priya: The intermittent 401 is usually either clock skew or the token scope. We sent a notes doc — link in chat: docs.redwood.com/nexa-health/onboard. The peering requires us to create the destination route on our side; if you share the subnet IDs we can open the peering from Redwood side and coordinate the handshake.
[01:28] Marcus: Ok i'll get those; expecting to have subnet IDs today but infra is slammed.

[01:34] Jordan: Great. On the bench results — Priya, can you summarise the runs you did with their test corpus last week?
[01:40] Priya: Sure. We ran three configs: hosted baseline, dedicated default fp16, and a quantized int8-ish run via our QAT profile. Latency median numbers: hosted was 210ms median on short prompts, dedicated fp16 around 95ms median, and int8-ish at 110ms median but cost per token dropped ~40%. There's some noise on longer sequences — the int8 variant shows larger variance due to token packing thresholds. I uploaded the bench sheet: drive.google.com/bench/nexa-v1 (short link).
[02:12] Lena: That's promising. Are those numbers on the exact model we anticipate for prod? We had asked for the 2.7B layer variant.
[02:22] Priya: These runs were on the 2.7B we onboarded, yes, but tuned with our default quant profile; we can try the lower-noise kernel selection and run a few repeats.
[02:34] Jordan: There was one noisy run where KV cache filling changed tail latency — we flagged it.
[02:38] Marcus: We noticed some memory spikes during the int8 runs on the dedicated pool. Could that be batch sizing?
[02:44] Priya: Yeah it's likely continuous batching sizing plus a few outlier prompts with big context. We can set per-request max_context and also enable adaptive batching thresholds. We'll send recommended defaults.

[03:05] Aisha: On cost, can you ballpark monthly for our expected 2M tokens/day? We need to compare to what we see on Bedrock.
[03:12] Jordan: Rough estimate — on dedicated with 40% latency/cost optimizations (cache + quant) you should expect around 20-30% cost reduction vs naive hosted, but exact numbers depend on hit-rate on prefix cache. We'll provide a sample cost sheet in the updated bench spreadsheet.
[03:34] Lena: Important for our finance team. Also we need to confirm data residency — logs should not leave our EU VPC.
[03:42] Jordan: For Private/Dedicated we can keep logs in your VPC; for hosted we have configurable retention. Priya, quick note on audit logs?
[03:51] Priya: We can push logs to your log sink via secure forwarder; we support pushing to S3, GCS, or a customer-managed endpoint. Audit events include token ids, route, model version, and error traces. We also support KMS integration for keys.

[04:10] Marcus: For the VPC peering, do you support cross-account VPC peering or need us to accept a peering?
[04:17] Priya: We do cross-account peering; typically Redwood initiates the peering and your infra accepts, or we can do the reverse. We'll share step-by-step.

[04:28] Jordan: Ok tuning — quantization and batching recommendations. Priya?
[04:33] Priya: Recommended path: start with int8-ish QAT profile but leave the final logits in fp16 to avoid hallucination regressions for sensitive prompts. Use per-route batching config: max_batch 16 for low latency, batch_timeout 12ms. Enable prefix KV cache for stable prefixes like system role and user history — that gave us 2x token throughput in earlier tests. We'll share a config snippet in the repo: docs.redwood.com/configs/nexa-default.json (link).
[05:05] Lena: If we see quality drops, what's our rollback path?
[05:09] Priya: Canary rollouts — you can route X% of traffic to quantized variant and monitor eval metrics. Redwood Optimize can run automated regression checks against your eval set and trigger rollbacks.

[05:28] Jordan: On evals — Lena, you said you'll share the 200 prompt eval set?
[05:32] Lena: Yes, finalizing it today, will upload to the shared drive. Want to set pass/fail thresholds on exactness and hallucination rate.
[05:40] Jordan: Perfect. We'll map those metrics to the quality dashboard.

[06:00] Priya: Quick note on the intermittent 401 Marcus mentioned — could also be the service account key lifetime. If you used a short-lived token, ensure the refresh flow is in place; we've seen teams forget the refresh endpoint.
[06:14] Marcus: Good call, I'll validate the exchange.

[06:20] Aisha: Security — is the SOC2 doc latest? Our compliance folks asked.
[06:24] Jordan: We have the SOC2 Type II pack, ISO docs, pen test summary. I can share the secure link — jordan.redwood.com/sec/nexa-pack — Priya will do a follow-up with the compliance liaison.
[06:38] Priya: Also SSO/SAML integration for the console — we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. If you want RBAC scoping for developer vs ops, we can send a sample policy.

[06:55] Marcus: For the dedicated pool we requested, what's the expected time to provision once we sign the reserved capacity?
[07:02] Jordan: Once contract's signed, typical lead time is 7-10 business days to spin up the reserved pool in your region. For POC/demo we can allocate a temporary pool within 48 hours, depending on capacity.
[07:18] Aisha: That helps for ramp planning.

[07:24] Lena: Quick question — when you say "int8-ish" is that a lossy quant or do you have per-layer knobs?
[07:30] Priya: We do per-layer quant controls; our QAT profile uses simulated quantization during calibration and allows you to tune per-layer scale. We'll include a recommended starting point that preserved alignment on our initial evals.

[07:50] Jordan: Ok let's pivot to concrete next runs: Priya to run the 1k sample E2E run on dedicated pool focusing on 95th percentile latency and tail. Priya, any blocking?
[07:59] Priya: Need the VPC peering or an open egress path to Redwood endpoints. If Marcus can update the peering ticket we can run sandbox dedicated. Also need the final eval set to run quality checks at the same time.
[08:15] Marcus: I'll push on infra to prioritize the peering — aiming EOD tomorrow.

[08:21] Aisha: For the cost estimates, will the bench sheet show per-token and per-request breakdown?
[08:26] Jordan: Yes, we'll include token-level cost, average tokens per request, cache hit-rate assumptions, and example monthly run-rate.

[08:36] Lena: Competitor note — finance asked us to compare to Bedrock pricing and Anthropic. Do you have a short delta doc?
[08:45] Jordan: We have a competitive note PDF; I'll share a redacted comparison vs Bedrock and Anthropic — link in chat. Keep in mind differences in feature parity, region availability, and SLA.

[09:00] Priya: One operational gotcha: for long-running sessions with KV cache, make sure you pin model version during a session to avoid cold-cache due to auto-roll. We'll document the sticky session config.

[09:16] Marcus: For auditability, will logs include full prompts or redacted? We need PII controls.
[09:22] Priya: Redaction is configurable; you can redact PII at the client or have Redwood redact before persisting logs. We support a regex-based redaction pipeline or a field-level config.

[09:40] Jordan: Wrap-up — recap of action items, timeline, and risks: main risk is VPC peering delay affects E2E run.

[09:50] Lena: Agree. Also quality regression risk with int8, but we have canary and rollback.

[09:58] Jordan: Final quick sync on dates: Jordan sends bench update and quant knobs by 2026-09-03; Marcus shares subnet IDs by 2026-09-02; Priya runs 1k E2E by 2026-09-06; Lena uploads eval set by 2026-09-04. We'll reconvene same time next week unless urgent.
[10:18] Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:21] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcription contains some imperfect words ("int8-ish" sometimes appears as "int ate ish" in raw), speaker labels simplified. Shared artifacts referenced: docs.redwood.com/nexa-health/onboard, drive.google.com/bench/nexa-v1, docs.redwood.com/configs/nexa-default.json, jordan.redwood.com/sec/nexa-pack.
